brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.evidence: piece full at (-1,0),(0,0),(1,0) on levels 0 and 1, joined by snaps and joint bolts; top covers cover:-1,0,1/0,0,1/1,0,1;full;top give a flat shelf surface (plus covers on the half bases).
drawer:0#-1,1#cut and drawer:0#0,1#cut on half-n bases at (-1,1,0) and (0,1,0); mesh check clear.
The configurator checks fit and collisions only, not structural strength; no load rating can be claimed or verified for this build. Physical load testing would be required.

finish.summary: Two-tier shelf unit: six full hex bases (three per level, stacked with snaps), two north-half bases at the front of level 0 each carrying a drawer on its cut face, joint bolts on every shared wall, and top covers forming the shelf surfaces. check_build: no rule errors, meshClash "clear". Open side faces could optionally take caps (info only).

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
